text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you stand regarding the Salāt, so neither play around with your beard, nor with your head, nor with the pebbles while you are praying Salāt, unless you prepare (pebbles) as you are about to do Sajdah, so it is not a problem’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَلَا تَعْبَثْ بِلِحْيَتِكَ وَ لَا بِرَأْسِكَ وَ لَا تَعْبَثْ بِالْحَصَى وَ أَنْتَ تُصَلِّي إِلَّا أَنْ تُسَوِّيَ حَيْثُ تَسْجُدُ فَإِنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you stand regarding the Salāt, so neither play around with your beard, nor with your head, nor with the pebbles while you are praying Salāt, unless you prepare (pebbles) as you are about to do Sajdah, so it is not a problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/79)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is befitting for the one who recites the Quran that when he passes by a Verse from the Quran wherein is a question or a caution, he should ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during that for goodness he hopes for, and ask Him<sup>azwj</sup> for the well-being, from the Fire and from the Punishment’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ إِذَا مَرَّ بِآيَةٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فِيهَا مَسْأَلَةٌ أَوْ تَخْوِيفٌ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَيْرَ مَا يَرْجُو وَ يَسْأَلَهُ الْعَافِيَةَ مِنَ النَّارِ وَ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is befitting for the one who recites the Quran that when he passes by a Verse from the Quran wherein is a question or a caution, he should ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during that for goodness he hopes for, and ask Him<sup>azwj</sup> for the well-being, from the Fire and from the Punishment’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/79)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Saeed Baya’a Al Sabiry who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man weep during the Salāt?’ So heasws said: ‘Congratulations! Congratulations, and even though it (tears) may be the like of the head of a fly’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ يَتَبَاكَى الرَّجُلُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَقَالَ بَخْ بَخْ وَ لَوْ مِثْلَ رَأْسِ الذُّبَابِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Saeed Baya’a Al Sabiry who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man weep during the Salāt?’ So heasws said: ‘Congratulations! Congratulations, and even though it (tears) may be the like of the head of a fly’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/79)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who happens to be with the prayer-leader who passes by the question or by a Verse wherein is the Mention of the Paradise or Fire. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it if he were to ask during that and seek Refuge from the Fire during the Salāt, and ask Allahazwj for the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ فَيَمُرُّ بِالْمَسْأَلَةِ أَوْ بِآيَةٍ فِيهَا ذِكْرُ جَنَّةٍ أَوْ نَارٍ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَسْأَلَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ يَتَعَوَّذَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ مِنَ النَّارِ وَ يَسْأَلَ اللَّهَ الْجَنَّةَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who happens to be with the prayer-leader who passes by the question or by a Verse wherein is the Mention of the Paradise or Fire. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it if he were to ask during that and seek Refuge from the Fire during the Salāt, and ask Allahazwj for the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/80)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about mentioning the Chapter from the Book to supplicate with during the Salāt, like [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Chapter 112)’. So heasws said: ‘When you were supplicating by it, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذِكْرِ السُّورَةِ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يَدْعُو بِهَا فِي الصَّلَاةِ مِثْلَ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ فَقَالَ إِذَا كُنْتَ تَدْعُو بِهَا فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about mentioning the Chapter from the Book to supplicate with during the Salāt, like [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Chapter 112)’. So heasws said: ‘When you were supplicating by it, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/80)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Everything what you speak to Allahazwj with during an Obligatory Salāt, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلُّ مَا كَلَّمْتَ اللَّهَ بِهِ فِي صَلَاةِ الْفَرِيضَةِ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Everything what you speak to Allahazwj with during an Obligatory Salāt, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/81)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Al Fazl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When Rasool-Allahsaww was Ascended with to the sky, so hesaww reached [52:4] the frequented House (Bayt Al-Mamour), and the Salāt presented itself, Jibraeelas called the Azān and the Iqamah. So Rasool-Allahsaww moved forward (to lead), and the Angels and the Prophetsas formed rows behind Muhammadsaww’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا أُسْرِيَ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَبَلَغَ الْبَيْتَ الْمَعْمُورَ وَ حَضَرَتِ الصَّلَاةُ فَأَذَّنَ جَبْرَئِيلُ وَ أَقَامَ فَتَقَدَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ صَفَّ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَ النَّبِيُّونَ خَلْفَ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Al Fazl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When Rasool-Allahsaww was Ascended with to the sky, so hesaww reached [52:4] the frequented House (Bayt Al-Mamour), and the Salāt presented itself, Jibraeelas called the Azān and the Iqamah. So Rasool-Allahsaww moved forward (to lead), and the Angels and the Prophetsas formed rows behind Muhammadsaww’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/81)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Jibraeelas descended with the Azān upon Rasool-Allahsaww, hissaww head was on the lap of Aliasws. So Jibraeelas called the Azān and the Iqamah, Rasool-Allahsaww took notice and said: ‘O Aliasws! Did youasws hear?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. Hesaww said: ‘Did youasws memorise?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. Hesaww said: ‘Call Bilal and teach him’. So Aliasws called Bilal and taught him’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا هَبَطَ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) بِالْأَذَانِ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ رَأْسُهُ فِي حِجْرِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَذَّنَ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَقَامَ فَلَمَّا انْتَبَهَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ يَا عَلِيُّ سَمِعْتَ قَالَ نَعَمْ قَالَ حَفِظْتَ قَالَ نَعَمْ قَالَ ادْعُ بِلَالًا فَعَلِّمْهُ فَدَعَا عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) بِلَالًا فَعَلَّمَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Jibraeelas descended with the Azān upon Rasool-Allahsaww, hissaww head was on the lap of Aliasws. So Jibraeelas called the Azān and the Iqamah, Rasool-Allahsaww took notice and said: ‘O Aliasws! Did youasws hear?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. Hesaww said: ‘Did youasws memorise?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. Hesaww said: ‘Call Bilal and teach him’. So Aliasws called Bilal and taught him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/82)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘The Azān and the Iqamah are thirty five letters (sentences)’, and heasws numbered these by hisasws hand, one by one, the Azān being of eighteen letters (sentences), and the Iqamah being of seventeen letters (sentences)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْأَذَانُ وَ الْإِقَامَةُ خَمْسَةٌ وَ ثَلَاثُونَ حَرْفاً فَعَدَّ ذَلِكَ بِيَدِهِ وَاحِداً وَاحِداً الْأَذَانَ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفاً وَ الْإِقَامَةَ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘The Azān and the Iqamah are thirty five letters (sentences)’, and heasws numbered these by hisasws hand, one by one, the Azān being of eighteen letters (sentences), and the Iqamah being of seventeen letters (sentences)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/82)

text: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Azān is twice by twice, and the Iqamah is twice by twice’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْأَذَانُ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى وَ الْإِقَامَةُ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Azān is twice by twice, and the Iqamah is twice by twice’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/82)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘O Zurara! Open the Azān with exclamations of four Takbīrs, and end it with exclamations of two Takbīrs and two Extollations (of Oneness)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ يَا زُرَارَةُ تَفْتَتِحُ الْأَذَانَ بِأَرْبَعِ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَ تَخْتِمُهُ بِتَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ وَ تَهْلِيلَتَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘O Zurara! Open the Azān with exclamations of four Takbīrs, and end it with exclamations of two Takbīrs and two Extollations (of Oneness)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/83)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the yawning during the Azān and the Iqamah, so heasws said: ‘Weasws do not recognise (experience) it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ التَّثْوِيبِ فِي الْأَذَانِ وَ الْإِقَامَةِ فَقَالَ مَا نَعْرِفُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the yawning during the Azān and the Iqamah, so heasws said: ‘Weasws do not recognise (experience) it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/83)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘When you recite the Azān, so be eloquent with the ‘Alif’ and the ‘Ha’ (two letters of the Arabic Alphabet), and send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww every time you mention it, or a mentioner mentions it during an Azān or an Iqamah’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ فَأَفْصِحْ بِالْأَلِفِ وَ الْهَاءِ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ كُلَّمَا ذَكَرْتَهُ أَوْ ذَكَرَهُ ذَاكِرٌ فِي أَذَانٍ وَ غَيْرِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘When you recite the Azān, so be eloquent with the ‘Alif’ and the ‘Ha’ (two letters of the Arabic Alphabet), and send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww every time you mention it, or a mentioner mentions it during an Azān or an Iqamah’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/84)

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you recite an Azān and an Iqamah, two rows of Angels pray Salāt behind you, and when you recite an Iqamah, one row of the Angels pray Salāt behind you’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ وَ أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفَّانِ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَ إِذَا أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفٌّ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you recite an Azān and an Iqamah, two rows of Angels pray Salāt behind you, and when you recite an Iqamah, one row of the Angels pray Salāt behind you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/84)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws, said, ‘I asked himasws, ‘Would one Azān suffice me?’ Heasws said: ‘When you are praying Salāt in a Jam’at, it would not suffice you except for an Azān and an Iqamah; but if you were alone initiating a matter fearing that it (Salāt) would be missed out by you, an Iqamah would suffice you, except for Al-Fajr and Al-Maghrib, for it is befitting that you recite an Azān regarding these two and an Iqamah due to the reason that there is no shortening in these two just as you would shorten in the rest of the Salāts’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ أَ يُجْزِئُ أَذَانٌ وَاحِدٌ قَالَ إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ جَمَاعَةً لَمْ يُجْزِئْ إِلَّا أَذَانٌ وَ إِقَامَةٌ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ تُبَادِرُ أَمْراً تَخَافُ أَنْ يَفُوتَكَ يُجْزِئُكَ إِقَامَةٌ إِلَّا الْفَجْرَ وَ الْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُؤَذِّنَ فِيهِمَا وَ تُقِيمَ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّهُ لَا يَقْصُرُ فِيهِمَا كَمَا يَقْصُرُ فِي سَائِرِ الصَّلَوَاتِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws, said, ‘I asked himasws, ‘Would one Azān suffice me?’ Heasws said: ‘When you are praying Salāt in a Jam’at, it would not suffice you except for an Azān and an Iqamah; but if you were alone initiating a matter fearing that it (Salāt) would be missed out by you, an Iqamah would suffice you, except for Al-Fajr and Al-Maghrib, for it is befitting that you recite an Azān regarding these two and an Iqamah due to the reason that there is no shortening in these two just as you would shorten in the rest of the Salāts’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/84)

text: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Nasr who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man speak during the Azān?’ Heasws said: ‘No problem’. I said, ‘During the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ يَتَكَلَّمُ الرَّجُلُ فِي الْأَذَانِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ قُلْتُ فِي الْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Nasr who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man speak during the Azān?’ Heasws said: ‘No problem’. I said, ‘During the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/85)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said, ‘There is no problem if the man were to recite the Azān without being in ablution, but he cannot recite an Iqamah unless he was upon an ablution’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَ لَا يُقِيمُ إِلَّا وَ هُوَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said, ‘There is no problem if the man were to recite the Azān without being in ablution, but he cannot recite an Iqamah unless he was upon an ablution’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/85)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who ends up to the prayer leader when he is greeting. Heasws said: ‘It is not upon him that he should repeat the Azān. So let him enter along with them in their Azān. So if he were to find them to have dispersed, he should repeat the Azān’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنْتَهِي إِلَى الْإِمَامِ حِينَ يُسَلِّمُ قَالَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الْأَذَانَ فَلْيَدْخُلْ مَعَهُمْ فِي أَذَانِهِمْ فَإِنْ وَجَدَهُمْ قَدْ تَفَرَّقُوا أَعَادَ الْأَذَانَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who ends up to the prayer leader when he is greeting. Heasws said: ‘It is not upon him that he should repeat the Azān. So let him enter along with them in their Azān. So if he were to find them to have dispersed, he should repeat the Azān’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/86)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabaty, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about the Azān, ‘Is it allowed if it happens to be from someone without understanding?’ Heasws said: ‘No! The Azān is not correct, and it is not allowed that the Azān be recited except by an understanding Muslim man. So if he knows the Azān, so he can recite with it, but if he does not happen to be understanding, his Azān is not allowed, nor is his Iqamah, nor should he be followed with (in the Jam’atal Salāt)’. And heasws was asked about the man who recites an Azān and an Iqamah in order to pray Salāt alone. So another man comes over and is saying to him, ‘We should pray together’. So is it allowed that he should pray Salāt with that Azān and the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should recite an Azān and an Iqamah’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنِ الْأَذَانِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عَارِفٍ قَالَ لَا يَسْتَقِيمُ الْأَذَانُ وَ لَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ بِهِ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ مُسْلِمٌ عَارِفٌ فَإِنْ عَلِمَ الْأَذَانَ فَأَذَّنَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَارِفاً لَمْ يُجْزِ أَذَانُهُ وَ لَا إِقَامَتُهُ وَ لَا يُقْتَدَى بِهِ وَ سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ لِيُصَلِّيَ وَحْدَهُ فَيَجِي‏ءُ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَيَقُولُ لَهُ نُصَلِّي جَمَاعَةً فَهَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَا بِذَلِكَ الْأَذَانِ وَ الْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنْ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabaty, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about the Azān, ‘Is it allowed if it happens to be from someone without understanding?’ Heasws said: ‘No! The Azān is not correct, and it is not allowed that the Azān be recited except by an understanding Muslim man. So if he knows the Azān, so he can recite with it, but if he does not happen to be understanding, his Azān is not allowed, nor is his Iqamah, nor should he be followed with (in the Jam’atal Salāt)’. And heasws was asked about the man who recites an Azān and an Iqamah in order to pray Salāt alone. So another man comes over and is saying to him, ‘We should pray together’. So is it allowed that he should pray Salāt with that Azān and the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should recite an Azān and an Iqamah’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/86)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding the man who forgets the Azān and the Iqamah until he enters into the Salāt. Heasws said: ‘If he remembers before he recites, so let him send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww and let him recite Iqamah; and if it was so that he had already (started the) recitation, so let him complete his Salāt’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى الْأَذَانَ وَ الْإِقَامَةَ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ ذَكَرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فَلْيُصَلِّ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ لْيُقِمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ قَرَأَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلَاتَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding the man who forgets the Azān and the Iqamah until he enters into the Salāt. Heasws said: ‘If he remembers before he recites, so let him send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww and let him recite Iqamah; and if it was so that he had already (started the) recitation, so let him complete his Salāt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/87)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who errs in the Azān, so he brings forward or delays (a sentence), he should return to the former which he had delayed until he completes upon its ending’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ سَهَا فِي الْأَذَانِ فَقَدَّمَ أَوْ أَخَّرَ عَادَ عَلَى الْأَوَّلِ الَّذِي أَخَّرَهُ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ عَلَى آخِرِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who errs in the Azān, so he brings forward or delays (a sentence), he should return to the former which he had delayed until he completes upon its ending’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/88)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘The man can recite the Azān while he is seated, but he cannot recite the Iqamah until he is standing; and you can recite the Azān while you are riding but you cannot recite Iqamah until you are upon the ground’.

citation.arabic_text: يُؤَذِّنُ الرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ لَا يُقِمْ إِلَّا وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ تُؤَذِّنُ وَ أَنْتَ رَاكِبٌ وَ لَا تُقِمْ إِلَّا وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘The man can recite the Azān while he is seated, but he cannot recite the Iqamah until he is standing; and you can recite the Azān while you are riding but you cannot recite Iqamah until you are upon the ground’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/89)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘Can the man recite the Azān and he is upon other than the Qiblah?’ Heasws said: ‘If it was so that the testimonies were borne facing the Qiblah, there would be no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ يُؤَذِّنُ الرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ إِذَا كَانَ التَّشَهُّدُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘Can the man recite the Azān and he is upon other than the Qiblah?’ Heasws said: ‘If it was so that the testimonies were borne facing the Qiblah, there would be no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/89)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the woman, ‘Is there a recitation of an Azān and an Iqamah upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْمَرْأَةِ عَلَيْهَا أَذَانٌ وَ إِقَامَةٌ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the woman, ‘Is there a recitation of an Azān and an Iqamah upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/89)

text: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘An Iqamah of the woman is that she exclaims Takbīr and testifies that there is no god except for Allahazwj and that Muhammadsaww is Hisazwj servant and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِقَامَةُ الْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تُكَبِّرَ وَ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘An Iqamah of the woman is that she exclaims Takbīr and testifies that there is no god except for Allahazwj and that Muhammadsaww is Hisazwj servant and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/89)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abu Haroun Al Makfouf who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O Abu Haroun! The Iqamah is from the Salāt. So when you establish it, so neither speak nor gesture with your hands’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَا أَبَا هَارُونَ الْإِقَامَةُ مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ فَإِذَا أَقَمْتَهُ فَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ وَ لَا تُومِ بِيَدِكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abu Haroun Al Makfouf who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O Abu Haroun! The Iqamah is from the Salāt. So when you establish it, so neither speak nor gesture with your hands’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/90)

text: And by this chain, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘None of you should recite an Iqamah for the Salāt while he is walking, nor while riding, nor lying down, unless he happens to be sick; and let him be able upon regarding the Iqamah just as he is able upon regarding the Salāt. So when he takes to the Iqamah, so he is in the Salāt’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقِمْ أَحَدُكُمُ الصَّلَاةَ وَ هُوَ مَاشٍ وَ لَا رَاكِبٌ وَ لَا مُضْطَجِعٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَرِيضاً وَ لْيَتَمَكَّنْ فِي الْإِقَامَةِ كَمَا يَتَمَكَّنُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا أَخَذَ فِي الْإِقَامَةِ فَهُوَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘None of you should recite an Iqamah for the Salāt while he is walking, nor while riding, nor lying down, unless he happens to be sick; and let him be able upon regarding the Iqamah just as he is able upon regarding the Salāt. So when he takes to the Iqamah, so he is in the Salāt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/90)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man enters the Masjid and he is not accomplishing it with his companions, and there remains upon the prayer-leader, either a Verse or two Verses, so he fears that if he were to recite an Azān and an Iqamah, he (the prayer-leader) would go into Rukū (a bowing), so let him say, ‘The Salāt has been established! Allahazwj is the Greatest! Allahazwj is the Greatest! There is no god except for Allahazwj!’, and let him enter into the Salāt’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ الْمَسْجِدَ وَ هُوَ لَا يَأْتَمُّ بِصَاحِبِهِ وَ قَدْ بَقِيَ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ آيَةٌ أَوْ آيَتَانِ فَخَشِيَ إِنْ هُوَ أَذَّنَ وَ أَقَامَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ فَلْيَقُلْ قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ لْيَدْخُلْ فِي الصَّلَاةِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man enters the Masjid and he is not accomplishing it with his companions, and there remains upon the prayer-leader, either a Verse or two Verses, so he fears that if he were to recite an Azān and an Iqamah, he (the prayer-leader) would go into Rukū (a bowing), so let him say, ‘The Salāt has been established! Allahazwj is the Greatest! Allahazwj is the Greatest! There is no god except for Allahazwj!’, and let him enter into the Salāt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/90)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Bin Ali Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Azān before Al-Fajr, so heasws said: ‘When it was in a Jam’at, so no, and when he was alone, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْأَذَانِ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَلَا وَ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Bin Ali Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Azān before Al-Fajr, so heasws said: ‘When it was in a Jam’at, so no, and when he was alone, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/90)

text: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘There is sitting between the Azān and the Iqamah in all Salāts, provided other Salāt is not performed before Iqamah’.

citation.arabic_text: الْقُعُودُ بَيْنَ الْأَذَانِ وَ الْإِقَامَةِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ كُلِّهَا إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ قَبْلَ الْإِقَامَةِ صَلَاةٌ يُصَلِّيهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘There is sitting between the Azān and the Iqamah in all Salāts, provided other Salāt is not performed before Iqamah’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/91)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from one of our companions, from Ismail Bin Jabir that, ‘Abu Abdullahasws would recite an Azān, and someone else would recite the Iqamah, and he said, ‘When heasws recited the Iqamah, someone else would recite the Azān’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ يُقِيمُ وَ قَدْ أَذَّنَ غَيْرُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from one of our companions, from Ismail Bin Jabir that, ‘Abu Abdullahasws would recite an Azān, and someone else would recite the Iqamah, and he said, ‘When heasws recited the Iqamah, someone else would recite the Azān’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/91)

text: A group of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sariy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Azān is recited slowly, but the Iqamah, flowingly’.

citation.arabic_text: الْأَذَانُ تَرْتِيلٌ وَ الْإِقَامَةُ حَدْرٌ .
citation.translation: A group of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sariy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Azān is recited slowly, but the Iqamah, flowingly’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, raising it, ‘Heasws said: ‘On the Day of Judgement, three would be upon dunes of Musk – one of them a Muezzin reciting Azān in anticipation (of the Rewards of Allahazwj)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ ثَلَاثَةٌ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَلَى كُثْبَانِ الْمِسْكِ أَحَدُهُمْ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَذَّنَ احْتِسَاباً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, raising it, ‘Heasws said: ‘On the Day of Judgement, three would be upon dunes of Musk – one of them a Muezzin reciting Azān in anticipation (of the Rewards of Allahazwj)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/92)

text: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Muezzin, there would seek Forgiveness for him (everything) up to the extent of his voice, and there would testify for him everything which hears it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْمُؤَذِّنُ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ مَدَى صَوْتِهِ وَ يَشْهَدُ لَهُ كُلُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ سَمِعَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Muezzin, there would seek Forgiveness for him (everything) up to the extent of his voice, and there would testify for him everything which hears it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/92)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww, whenever hesaww heard a Muezzin, recited Azān (along with him), saying similar to what he was saying, in everything’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا سَمِعَ الْمُؤَذِّنَ يُؤَذِّنُ قَالَ مِثْلَ مَا يَقُولُهُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww, whenever hesaww heard a Muezzin, recited Azān (along with him), saying similar to what he was saying, in everything’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/93)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira Al Nazary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who hears a Muezzin saying, ‘I testify that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, so he says, ratifying, anticipating (Rewards), ‘And I testify that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and I suffice with these two from the ones who refuse and fight against, and I view with these two (testimonies)’. The one who acknowledges and testifies, would have for him from the Recompense, the number of the ones who denied and rejected, and (as well as) the likes of the number of the ones who acknowledged and recognised’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ سَمِعَ الْمُؤَذِّنَ يَقُولُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اللَّهِ فَقَالَ مُصَدِّقاً مُحْتَسِباً وَ أَنَا أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ أَكْتَفِي بِهِمَا عَمَّنْ أَبَى وَ جَحَدَ وَ أُعِينُ بِهِمَا مَنْ أَقَرَّ وَ شَهِدَ كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ عَدَدُ مَنْ أَنْكَرَ وَ جَحَدَ وَ مِثْلُ عَدَدِ مَنْ أَقَرَّ وَ عَرَفَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira Al Nazary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who hears a Muezzin saying, ‘I testify that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, so he says, ratifying, anticipating (Rewards), ‘And I testify that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and I suffice with these two from the ones who refuse and fight against, and I view with these two (testimonies)’. The one who acknowledges and testifies, would have for him from the Recompense, the number of the ones who denied and rejected, and (as well as) the likes of the number of the ones who acknowledged and recognised’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/93)

text: Ali Bin Muhammd, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The height of the wall of Masjid of Rasool-Allahsaww was of one stature. So hesaww was saying to Bilal: ‘When the time comes, O Bilal, climb above the wall and raise your voice with the Azān, for Allahazwj has Allocated a wind with the Azān raising it to the sky, and that the Angels, when they are hearing the Azān from the inhabitants of the earth, they are saying: ‘Voices of the community of Muhammadsaww (affirming) the Oneness of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’, and they are seeking Forgiveness for the community of Muhammadsaww until they are free from that Salāt’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ طُولُ حَائِطِ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَامَةً فَكَانَ يَقُولُ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِبِلَالٍ إِذَا دَخَلَ الْوَقْتُ يَا بِلَالُ اعْلُ فَوْقَ الْجِدَارِ وَ ارْفَعْ صَوْتَكَ بِالْأَذَانِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ وَكَّلَ بِالْأَذَانِ رِيحاً تَرْفَعُهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ إِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ إِذَا سَمِعُوا الْأَذَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا هَذِهِ أَصْوَاتُ أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِتَوْحِيدِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِأُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حَتَّى يَفْرُغُوا مِنْ تِلْكَ الصَّلَاةِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammd, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The height of the wall of Masjid of Rasool-Allahsaww was of one stature. So hesaww was saying to Bilal: ‘When the time comes, O Bilal, climb above the wall and raise your voice with the Azān, for Allahazwj has Allocated a wind with the Azān raising it to the sky, and that the Angels, when they are hearing the Azān from the inhabitants of the earth, they are saying: ‘Voices of the community of Muhammadsaww (affirming) the Oneness of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’, and they are seeking Forgiveness for the community of Muhammadsaww until they are free from that Salāt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/94)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Husayn Bin Asad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Yaqzaan, (It has been narrated) raising it to themasws having said: ‘The man should be saying when he is free from reciting the Azān and is seated, ‘O Allahazwj! Make my heart to be righteous, and my livelihood to be constant, and my sustenance to be continuous, and Make for me, in the presence of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, a dwelling and a rest’.

citation.arabic_text: يَقُولُ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ الْأَذَانِ وَ جَلَسَ اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ قَلْبِي بَارّاً وَ عَيْشِي قَارّاً وَ رِزْقِي دَارّاً وَ اجْعَلْ لِي عِنْدَ قَبْرِ نَبِيِّكَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَرَاراً وَ مُسْتَقَرّاً .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Husayn Bin Asad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Yaqzaan, (It has been narrated) raising it to themasws having said: ‘The man should be saying when he is free from reciting the Azān and is seated, ‘O Allahazwj! Make my heart to be righteous, and my livelihood to be constant, and my sustenance to be continuous, and Make for me, in the presence of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, a dwelling and a rest’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/94)

text: Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Rashid who said, ‘Hisham Bin Ibrahim narrated to me that he complained to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws of an illness and there is child being born for him. So heasws ordered him that he should raise his voice in the Azān in his house. He said, ‘I did so, and Allahazwj Removed my illness from me and my children were many’. Muhammad Bin Rashid (the narrator) said, ‘And I used to be with the illness all the time not having benefitted from it myself and a group of my servant and my family members. So when I heard that from Hisham, I acted upon it and Allahazwj Removed the illness from me and from my family members’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ أَنَّهُ شَكَا إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) سُقْمَهُ وَ أَنَّهُ لَا يُولَدُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ صَوْتَهُ بِالْأَذَانِ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَأَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَنِّي سُقْمِي وَ كَثُرَ وَلَدِي قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ وَ كُنْتُ دَائِمَ الْعِلَّةِ مَا أَنْفَكُّ مِنْهَا فِي نَفْسِي وَ جَمَاعَةِ خَدَمِي وَ عِيَالِي فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ هِشَامٍ عَمِلْتُ بِهِ فَأَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَنِّي وَ عَنْ عِيَالِيَ الْعِلَلَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Rashid who said, ‘Hisham Bin Ibrahim narrated to me that he complained to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws of an illness and there is child being born for him. So heasws ordered him that he should raise his voice in the Azān in his house. He said, ‘I did so, and Allahazwj Removed my illness from me and my children were many’. Muhammad Bin Rashid (the narrator) said, ‘And I used to be with the illness all the time not having benefitted from it myself and a group of my servant and my family members. So when I heard that from Hisham, I acted upon it and Allahazwj Removed the illness from me and from my family members’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/95)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘If a Muezzin were to repeat in the testimonies, and in ‘Hasten to the Salāt’, or ‘Hasten to the success’, twice or thrice, and more from that, when it was so that he intended by it the gathering of the people in order to gather them (more), there would be no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَوْ أَنَّ مُؤَذِّناً أَعَادَ فِي الشَّهَادَةِ وَ فِي حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ أَوْ حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ الْمَرَّتَيْنِ وَ الثَّلَاثَ وَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ بِهِ جَمَاعَةَ الْقَوْمِ لِيَجْمَعَهُمْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهِ بَأْسٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘If a Muezzin were to repeat in the testimonies, and in ‘Hasten to the Salāt’, or ‘Hasten to the success’, twice or thrice, and more from that, when it was so that he intended by it the gathering of the people in order to gather them (more), there would be no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/95)

text: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I hear himasws saying: ‘Recite Azān in your house for it would repel the Satanla, and it is recommended for the reason of the children’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ أَذِّنْ فِي بَيْتِكَ فَإِنَّهُ يَطْرُدُ الشَّيْطَانَ وَ يُسْتَحَبُّ مِنْ أَجْلِ الصِّبْيَانِ .
citation.translation: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I hear himasws saying: ‘Recite Azān in your house for it would repel the Satanla, and it is recommended for the reason of the children’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/96)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed Al Rashidy, from Yunus, (It has been narrated) from them<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The superior act during entering the Masjid is that you begin with your right foot when you enter, and with your left foot when you exit’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ الْفَضْلُ فِي دُخُولِ الْمَسْجِدِ أَنْ تَبْدَأَ بِرِجْلِكَ الْيُمْنَى إِذَا دَخَلْتَ وَ بِالْيُسْرَى إِذَا خَرَجْتَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed Al Rashidy, from Yunus, (It has been narrated) from them<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The superior act during entering the Masjid is that you begin with your right foot when you enter, and with your left foot when you exit’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/96)

text: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you enter the Masjid, so send Blessings (Salawat) upon the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>; and when you exit, so do that (as well)’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْمَسْجِدَ فَصَلِّ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ إِذَا خَرَجْتَ فَافْعَلْ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you enter the Masjid, so send Blessings (Salawat) upon the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>; and when you exit, so do that (as well)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/96)

text: And from him, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban and Muawiya Bin Wahab who both said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you stand to the Salāt, so say, ‘O Allahazwj! I consider Muhammadsaww in front of me in Yourazwj Presence along with me wishes and needs and I turn to You through themasws. therefore Make it for me a valid reason in Yourazwj Presence, in the world and in the Hereafter, to be of the ones of proximity. Make my Salāt to be Acceptable through himsaww, and my sins to be Forgiven through himsaww, and my supplications to be Answered through himsaww, Youazwj are the Forgiver, Merciful’.

citation.arabic_text: ا قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَقُلِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُقَدِّمُ إِلَيْكَ مُحَمَّداً ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَيْنَ يَدَيْ حَاجَتِي وَ أَتَوَجَّهُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ فَاجْعَلْنِي بِهِ وَجِيهاً عِنْدَكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ وَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ اجْعَلْ صَلَاتِي بِهِ مَقْبُولَةً وَ ذَنْبِي بِهِ مَغْفُوراً وَ دُعَائِي بِهِ مُسْتَجَاباً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ .
citation.translation: And from him, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban and Muawiya Bin Wahab who both said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you stand to the Salāt, so say, ‘O Allahazwj! I consider Muhammadsaww in front of me in Yourazwj Presence along with me wishes and needs and I turn to You through themasws. therefore Make it for me a valid reason in Yourazwj Presence, in the world and in the Hereafter, to be of the ones of proximity. Make my Salāt to be Acceptable through himsaww, and my sins to be Forgiven through himsaww, and my supplications to be Answered through himsaww, Youazwj are the Forgiver, Merciful’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/96)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Hashimy, from Abu Hafs Al Attar, a Sheykh from the people of Al Medina who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Whenever one of you prays the Prescribed Salāt and exits from the Masjid, so let him pause by the door, then let him say, ‘O Allahazwj! Youazwj Called me, so I answered Yourazwj Call, and I prayed the Prescribed Salāts, and I spread out in spread out in Yourazwj earth just as Youazwj Commanded me. So I ask Youazwj from Yourazwj Grace, the working in Yourazwj obedience, and keeping aside from Yourazwj Anger, and sufficiency of the sustenance by Yourazwj Mercy’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا صَلَّى أَحَدُكُمُ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ وَ خَرَجَ مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ فَلْيَقِفْ بِبَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ لْيَقُلِ اللَّهُمَّ دَعَوْتَنِي فَأَجَبْتُ دَعْوَتَكَ وَ صَلَّيْتُ مَكْتُوبَتَكَ وَ انْتَشَرْتُ فِي أَرْضِكَ كَمَا أَمَرْتَنِي فَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَمَلَ بِطَاعَتِكَ وَ اجْتِنَابَ سَخَطِكَ وَ الْكَفَافَ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ بِرَحْمَتِكَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Hashimy, from Abu Hafs Al Attar, a Sheykh from the people of Al Medina who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Whenever one of you prays the Prescribed Salāt and exits from the Masjid, so let him pause by the door, then let him say, ‘O Allahazwj! Youazwj Called me, so I answered Yourazwj Call, and I prayed the Prescribed Salāts, and I spread out in spread out in Yourazwj earth just as Youazwj Commanded me. So I ask Youazwj from Yourazwj Grace, the working in Yourazwj obedience, and keeping aside from Yourazwj Anger, and sufficiency of the sustenance by Yourazwj Mercy’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (15/97)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Raise your hands during the opening of the Salāt opposite your face but do not raise them all the way’.

citation.arabic_text: تَرْفَعُ يَدَيْكَ فِي افْتِتَاحِ الصَّلَاةِ قُبَالَةَ وَجْهِكَ وَ لَا تَرْفَعْهُمَا كُلَّ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Raise your hands during the opening of the Salāt opposite your face but do not raise them all the way’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (5/97)

text: And from him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When you stand regarding the Salāt and you exclaim Takbīr, so raise your hands, and your palms should not exceed your ears, i.e. parallel to your cheeks’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَكَبَّرْتَ فَارْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ وَ لَا تُجَاوِزْ بِكَفَّيْكَ أُذُنَيْكَ أَيْ حِيَالَ خَدَّيْكَ .
citation.translation: And from him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When you stand regarding the Salāt and you exclaim Takbīr, so raise your hands, and your palms should not exceed your ears, i.e. parallel to your cheeks’.

text: From him, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘The lowest of what would suffice from the exclamation of Takbīr during the direction, is one Takbīr; and three Takbīrs are better, and seven would be superior’.

citation.arabic_text: أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِئُ مِنَ التَّكْبِيرِ فِي التَّوَجُّهِ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ ثَلَاثُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ أَحْسَنُ وَ سَبْعٌ أَفْضَلُ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘The lowest of what would suffice from the exclamation of Takbīr during the direction, is one Takbīr; and three Takbīrs are better, and seven would be superior’.

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you are a prayer-leader, one exclamation of Takbīr would suffice you, because there would be with you ones with the need, and the weakness, and the old age’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً أَجْزَأَتْكَ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ لِأَنَّ مَعَكَ ذَا الْحَاجَةِ وَ الضَّعِيفَ وَ الْكَبِيرَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The exclamation of Takbīr regarding the five Obligatory Salāts are ninety five exclamations of Takbīrs – from these, the Takbīrs for the Qunoot are five’.

citation.arabic_text: التَّكْبِيرُ فِي صَلَاةِ الْفَرْضِ الْخَمْسِ الصَّلَوَاتِ خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَاتُ الْقُنُوتِ خَمْسَةٌ .

text: And it is reported as well, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al-Mugheira, ‘And heasws explained these – In Al-Zohr there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Asr there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Maghrib there are sixteen exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Isha the last there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Fajr there are eleven exclamations of Takbīr, and there are five Takbīrs of the Qunoot in the five Salāts’.

citation.arabic_text: الظُّهْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْعَصْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْفَجْرِ إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتِ الْقُنُوتِ فِي خَمْسِ صَلَوَاتٍ .
citation.translation: And it is reported as well, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al-Mugheira, ‘And heasws explained these – In Al-Zohr there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Asr there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Maghrib there are sixteen exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Isha the last there are twenty one exclamations of Takbīr, and in Al-Fajr there are eleven exclamations of Takbīr, and there are five Takbīrs of the Qunoot in the five Salāts’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When you open the Salāt, so raise your palms, then extend them with an extension. Then exclaim three Takbīrs, then say, ‘O Allahazwj! Youazwj are the King, the Truth. There is no god except for Youazwj. Glory be to Youazwj. I have been unjust to myself, therefore Forgive my sins for me, for no one forgives the sins except for Youazwj’. Then exclaim two Takbīrs, then say, ‘Here I am and at Yourazwj service, and the goodness is in Yourazwj Hands, and the evil is not to Youazwj, and the Guided one is the one whom Youazwj Guide. There is no Shelter (apart) from Youazwj except to Youazwj. Glory be to Youazwj, and Tender are Youazwj, and Blessed, and Exalted. Glory be to Youazwj, Lordazwj of the House!’ Then exclaim two Takbīrs, then you should be saying, ‘I divert my face to the One Who Originated the skies and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, with uprightness and submissiveness, and I am not from the Polytheists. My Salāt, and my rituals, and my life, and my death are for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds. There is no associate for Youazwj, and by that I am Commanded, and I am from the Muslims’. Then seek Refuge from the Pelted Satanla, then recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1)’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا افْتَتَحْتَ الصَّلَاةَ فَارْفَعْ كَفَّيْكَ ثُمَّ ابْسُطْهُمَا بَسْطاً ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ ثَلَاثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي إِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ ثُمَّ تُكَبِّرُ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قُلْ لَبَّيْكَ وَ سَعْدَيْكَ وَ الْخَيْرُ فِي يَدَيْكَ وَ الشَّرُّ لَيْسَ إِلَيْكَ وَ الْمَهْدِيُّ مَنْ هَدَيْتَ لَا مَلْجَأَ مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ سُبْحَانَكَ وَ حَنَانَيْكَ تَبَارَكْتَ وَ تَعَالَيْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ رَبَّ الْبَيْتِ ثُمَّ تُكَبِّرُ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَ الْأَرْضَ عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِماً وَ مَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَ نُسُكِي وَ مَحْيَايَ وَ مَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ بِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَ أَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثُمَّ تَعَوَّذْ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ ثُمَّ اقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ .
